svg.title: Proof. In cumulative coordinates, each interpolating simplex vertex differs from the normalized child by less than 1/M in each cumulative coordinate. The four original probability coordinates consequently differ by at most 2/M each. The l1/2 Lipschitz bound charges at most 4/M for the interpolation; child masses sum to one. For consecutive normals the half-gap has tangent at most 1/N, so any outer vertex has radius at most √
